A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the locus coeruleus (LC) is a brain region that has been implicated in many different aspects of stress and stress-related disease, and that chronic cold exposure (CCE), an animal model of chronic stress, has a profound effect on LC neurons.
chronic cold exposure potentiated the electrophysiologic effects of CRH on locus coeruleus (LC) neurons.
we have shown that cold stress potentiates the CRH response in the LC and that this potentiation is due to a decrease in the inhibitory GABAergic tone in this nucleus.

the locus coeruleus is a major player in the stress response, and that it is involved in the pathophysiology of depression and anxiety.
